traceability.notes:
All key requirements of docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md are implemented and exercised by targeted tests.
Core @implements functionality and format validation are present in the valid-annotation-format rule and supporting helpers, including parsing of story path plus one or more requirement IDs, strict format checks, and detailed error messaging when tokens are missing or malformed. Deep requirement validation for @implements is implemented in the valid-req-reference rule: it parses @implements lines, resolves each referenced story path to a file, caches and loads that story’s requirement IDs, and verifies that every ID on the @implements line exists in that specific story file. Failures correctly report both the missing reqId and the storyPath.
Backward compatibility and mixed-style support are preserved: existing @story and @req parsing and validation logic remain intact, and tests continue to verify legacy behavior. The new @implements flow is added alongside, not replacing, the older annotations. Mixed usage is explicitly tested at the format level (single comment with @story, @req, and @implements) and at the deep-validation level via handleAnnotationLine, which integrates @implements without disrupting @story/@req handling. Requirement IDs are scoped per story file, with dedicated fixtures demonstrating identical IDs in multiple stories validated independently.
The rule implementations follow ESLint best practices (separate helpers, clear meta and messages, RuleTester-based tests), and documentation plus ADR 010 describe the @implements behavior and rationale. Based on the concrete code and test evidence, this story’s acceptance criteria are fully satisfied.
